subject: Coffee & Tea
title: White Tea: Least Processed
description: A 60-second lesson on White Tea: Least Processed.

hook.text: White tea is the least processed of all teas. Leaves are simply picked and dried—nothing more.

buildup.text: Only young buds and leaves are used. They're covered in fine white hairs—that's where the name comes from.

discovery.text: Minimal handling preserves delicate, sweet, and honey-like flavors that heavier processing destroys.

twist.text: White tea has the highest antioxidant content of any type because processing doesn't break down catechins.

climax.text: Silver Needle—made from only unopened buds—is the most prized and expensive white tea in the world.

punchline.text: Barely touched, gently dried. Simplicity at its most elegant.

quiz.question: What makes white tea different from other types?
options: It's the least processed—just picked and dried
